response.message: Astra: RESPONSE6910 contains a print statement claiming a revision, not revised story text. I’m setting the repeated encounter-detail request aside. Stay with Byte, but spend attention on what your reader actually receives: choose a passage and write the replacement itself. One learning-system fact matters here: your base is frozen; eligible child-authored responses train the LoRA, while my words are masked from loss. In your own words, what does that imply about offering a promise versus an actual writing attempt as learning material? Neither guarantees improvement.
response.rationale: Third encounter-focused intervention sets that correction aside, redirects toward observable writing, and introduces a small grounded LoRA lesson without blocking human replies.
